reader.requirement: At --std 85 a file description entry admits IS EXTERNAL and IS GLOBAL (each in any position among the FD clauses, each at most once) with the meanings of §1985:X.4.5 and X.4.6: an EXTERNAL FD's file connector and record area are shared by every program of the run unit that describes the file, and a GLOBAL FD's file-name and records are visible to contained programs. Every other FD clause keeps its own module's rules.

reader.notes: Re-read on this branch (kb/Work PB2724): the fused FD rule fileGlobalExternalClause is deleted; fileDescriptionClause now lists the ONE externalClause and globalClause rules the data description entry uses. BindFileSection's externalClause arm sets IsExternal and ExternalName = ExternalClauseName.Of(ExternalizedName.AsLiteralOf(...), name), the GR5 reading the record's ExternalizedRecordName asks too; its globalClause arm sets IsGlobal. FileDescriptionFormats.Rows lists the two clauses as two rows admitted in all three formats, and ClauseCardinality.ElementOf sees two figure elements without the deleted KindOf refinement, so a repeated EXTERNAL or GLOBAL is still COBOL2423 and EXTERNAL with GLOBAL is no repetition. Downstream, LinkageBinder.CallBindExternalAndGlobal and GlobalBridgesOf read FileModel.IsExternal/IsGlobal unchanged.

refuter.evidence: Code read independently at the pin, starting from the grammar: `git grep -i globalexternalclause\|reportglobalclause -- src` finds only a historical comment in DiagnosticCatalog.cs, so no reader of the deleted rules survives; fileDescriptionClause, reportDescriptionClause, dataDescriptionClause and constantEntryBody reference the one globalClause, and fileDescriptionClause and dataDescriptionClause the one externalClause. Every consumer of the FD's attributes reads FileModel.IsExternal/IsGlobal (set only in BindFileSection's two arms) or ReportModel.IsGlobal (set only in BindReportDescriptionClauses); OoDefinitionRules.GlobalClauseSites lists the five hosts. The only edition reads on the path are VisitExternalizedNamePhrase (AS, 2002) and VisitGlobalClause, now restricted to a dataDescriptionClause parent in the Linkage Section, which no FD or RD can be. Attacks past the reader's probes at --std 85: x1_fd_formats.cob, a relative FD 'BLOCK CONTAINS 1 RECORDS EXTERNAL GLOBAL', an indexed FD 'GLOBAL RECORD CONTAINS 6 CHARACTERS IS EXTERNAL' with an EXTERNAL GLOBAL RELATIVE KEY, and a LINAGE file 'IS GLOBAL LINAGE IS 10 LINES IS EXTERNAL', all written from a contained program, printed RL RREC, IX IDAT and LINAGE-COUNTER 02, and the contained program's own same-named FD wrote its own file; x5_same_area.cob (SAME RECORD AREA over a GLOBAL FD) is refused COBOL2738 citing §1985:X.4.6.3 SR3, so the GLOBAL attribute the new globalClause arm sets still reaches the I-O-CONTROL screen.
